content:
PD-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE: High GPU queue growth and autoscaler failures in us-west-2-gpu-pool. Severity: P1. Alert: gpu-queue-length > 5000, autoscaler errors. Pager notified: Mike (oncall).

Mike (oncall): Acked. jumping in. any immediate customer impact?

Anya (sre): We're seeing queue growth on the inference queue (rl-infer) from ~600 requests/s to 8k/s over 18m. Throttles at the frontend started 12m ago. Some requests queued for >30s.

Samir (prod): Customer-facing dashboards show elevated latency for /v1/generate and a spike in 429s for two mid-market customers. Investigating scope.

Leo (infra): Autoscaler logs show repeated failures to provision nodes: "InstanceQuotaExceeded" then fallback. Autoscaler reported maxReplicas reached for gpu-pool (configured max 120).

Anya (sre): Also seeing scheduler logs indicating placement failures that led to stranded MIG slices. Example: "pod <rj-serve> cannot be placed: insufficient allocatable for MIG profile 1g. Node has free GPU capacity but in slices incompatible with pod request". Binpacking mismatch + MIG fragmentation.

Mike (oncall): So two problems: 1) cloud quota preventing scale-up, 2) fragmentation leaving usable GPU memory stranded. Which is dominant?

Anya (sre): Both. Autoscaler hit the scale cap (120). Cloud provider quota denies further. Meanwhile scheduler attempted to pack 1g pods but nodes were provisioned with mixed MIG configs (1g,2g,7g). Some nodes have leftover 0.5/1g slices unusable given pod shapes -> stranded capacity.

Samir (prod): Impact: 3 customers with heavy burst traffic seeing 30-80s tail latencies, some bulk embedding jobs queued. Estimated affected requests ~14k in queue.

Mike (oncall): Immediate mitigations?

Anya (sre): Short list:
- Emergency vertical fallback: route heavy traffic to smaller model variants temporarily (via router rule).
- Throttling rules: lower per-customer concurrency for affected customers.
- Manual rebalance: drain selected nodes and reprovision with consistent MIG profile to reduce fragmentation.
- Request emergency quota bump from cloud (already opened ticket).

Leo (infra): I'm starting a targeted node drain on 6 nodes that are highly fragmented. Plan: cordon -> drain -> reprovision as homogeneous MIG 1g slices. This should free a bunch of usable slots for current pod shapes. Doing this in waves (2 nodes at a time).

Mike (oncall): Please post commands and exactly which nodes. keep me in the loop.

Leo (infra): Running:
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-node-az1-12
kubectl drain gpu-node-az1-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
# reprovision (cloud CLI placeholder)
cloudctl compute resize gpu-node-az1-12 --mig-profile 1g
```
Will do waves at +5m intervals.

Anya (sre): Also toggled fallback routing to prefer tflite-smaller-variant for heavy lines:
```
POST /internal/router/config
{ "route": "/v1/generate", "policy": "prefer-model:tiny-1.1", "duration": "15m" }
```
This should cut token latencies and reduce queue inflow.

PD-bot: Incident note added: "Started node wave reprovisioning and routing fallback".

Mike (oncall): Any errors from the autoscaler after we started draining?

Leo (infra): Autoscaler still tries to scale up to replace drained nodes but cloud quota blocks some attempts:
```
E0708 14:02:13.123 autoscaler.go:245] provisioning failed: InstanceQuotaExceeded: requested 8 GPUs, allowed 0
```
Ticket with provider opened (TICKET-9921). Requesting emergency capacity.

Samir (prod): I've applied soft throttles on top customers (reduced concurrency by 40%). Early signs: inbound rate normalized to ~1.2k/s. Queue depth decreasing.

Anya (sre): After first two-node wave we reclaimed 16 usable 1g MIG slices, scheduler filled them immediately. Queue dropped ~22%. Still some pods failing placement due to mixed node profiles.

Mike (oncall): Good. Keep drips going. Any chance we can repack existing pods to fill holes without draining?

Leo (infra): We've attempted a repack job but eviction churn is heavy and kube-scheduler can't preempt nicely with MIG slices. A custom binpack tool might help but not in the short window. Manual drain/reprovision is fastest to consolidate slices.

Ops-bot: Cloud ticket update: TICKET-9921 status -> provisioning team responding, estimated 45-60m to approve emergency quota.

Anya (sre): Running a safety net: enable auto-fallback to cpu-backed small model for low-priority jobs and mark heavy requests for retry with jitter. Config snippet:
```
routes:
  - id: low-pri-fallback
    match: path_prefix:/v1/embeddings
    fallback_model: cpu-small
    retry_policy: { retries: 2, backoff: 500ms }
```

Samir (prod): Customer comms: drafting a status update. Notifying three customers: ACME-analytics, DataStreamCo, and EduPlat. Will include ETA for mitigation and ask to defer large bulk jobs.

Mike (oncall): Handing on-call to Leo for next 2h while I coordinate with product/Sales for customer updates. @Leo please take lead.

Leo (infra): Ack. taking over. continuing wave 2/3. next nodes: gpu-node-az2-03, gpu-node-az2-07.

(30m later)
Anya (sre): Update: we've reclaimed ~60 1g-equivalent slots across waves 1-3. Queue length down from 14k -> 2.1k. Throttles reduced. Baseline latency improving.

Ops-bot: Cloud ticket TICKET-9921 updated: capacity approved + 50 GPUs, being provisioned (eta 12m).

Samir (prod): Customer impact reduced to minor for all affected customers. ACME-analytics accepted temporary throttle. No data loss.

Leo (infra): After cloud capacity added, autoscaler scaled to needed size without error. We stopped the reprovision waves and left a plan to homogenize node fleet during low traffic window.

Mike (oncall): Great. Next steps / action items for postmortem:
- (Anya) Add regression test to detect MIG fragmentation patterns and early-warning metric (fragmentation ratio).
- (Leo) Auto-remediate script to convert mismatched MIG nodes during scale events.
- (Samir) Improve customer-facing rate-limit escalation doc and add automated notice when throttles hit threshold.
- (Infra) Re-evaluate maxReplicas cap and autoscaler backoff logic.

Anya (sre): Filing incident writeup and linking logs + kube-scheduler traces. Will include timeline.

PD-bot: Incident acknowledged resolved -> status: mitigated. Final note: root cause = mixed MIG profiles + autoscaler hitting configured max + cloud quota delay -> stranded GPU slices -> queue growth and throttling.

Mike (oncall): Thanks all. handing back to normal rotation. Will review postmortem early tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Leo (infra): Closing loop: plan to run a fleet homogenization during next low-traffic maintenance window and add automation to detect new nodes with incompatible MIG profiles.

Samir (prod): I'll send customer follow-ups and a summary for support.

Anya (sre): Adding one extra item: evaluate allowing autoscaler to overspill to a backup region as fallback (policy + costs).

PD-bot: Incident closed at ts 3130003600.
